{
  "candidate_rtl": "module addr_calcu(
    input [7:0] address,
    input [7:0] ptr1, ptr2,
    input [7:0] b,
    input control,
    output [15:0] count
);

    parameter [7:0] base = 8'b10000000;

    wire [7:0] selected_pointer;
    wire [7:0] q;
    wire q_nonzero;
    wire [7:0] csa_sum;
    wire [7:0] csa_carry;
    wire [9:0] total;
    wire negative_result;

    assign selected_pointer = control ? ptr1 : ptr2;

    // Mandatory modulo-256 intermediate. For base=8'h80,
    // this subtraction reduces to inverting pointer bit 7.
    assign q = selected_pointer - base;
    assign q_nonzero = |q;

    // Carry-save compression of three unsigned eight-bit operands.
    assign csa_sum = address ^ b ^ q;
    assign csa_carry = (address & b) |
                       (address & q) |
                       (b & q);
    assign total = {2'b00, csa_sum} + {1'b0, csa_carry, 1'b0};

    // offset = (-q) modulo 256.
    // Therefore count = total - (q_nonzero ? 256 : 0).
    // Its mathematical range is -255 through 510.
    assign negative_result = q_nonzero & ~total[9] & ~total[8];
    assign count = {{7{negative_result}},
                    (total[8] ^ q_nonzero), total[7:0]};

endmodule",
  "bottleneck": "The available evidence is the RTL dependency structure, not a mapped timing report. The original describes two pointer-dependent offset/subtract/add paths followed by an output selection. Pointer-derived arithmetic and carry propagation are plausible critical-path contributors, but Yosys may already merge or restructure these operations; the source alone does not establish serial mapped adder depth. There is no supplied evidence that control is uniquely late, and the stated constraints give it the same external delay as every other input.",
  "rewrite": "Select the pointer before arithmetic and define the eight-bit quantity q=(selected_pointer-base) modulo 256. Since offset=(-q) modulo 256, address+b-offset equals address+b+q minus 256 when q is nonzero, and equals address+b otherwise. At the default base, q generation is only an MSB inversion plus wiring. A bitwise carry-save compressor reduces address, b, and q to two operands for one final ten-bit carry-propagating addition. The subtraction of 256 is implemented entirely in the upper output bits, without another word-wide subtractor.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "A shorter maximum data arrival is plausible because the default-instance pointer negation/subtraction chain is replaced by a pointer mux, constant bit inversion, carry-save compression, and a final carry-propagating sum. The correction path uses a nonzero reduction and small upper-bit logic. No numerical gain is claimed: synthesis restructuring, mapped carry topology, mux placement, and correction-path loading may determine whether this beats the baseline. Measure maximum data arrival using the specified fixed Yosys/ABC/OpenSTA flow.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Sharing the arithmetic should provide area headroom relative to duplicated branches, while the compressor adds XOR/majority logic and the pointer mux moves onto the arithmetic input path. This is a hypothesis, not a measured area result. Accept this candidate only after full equivalence, mapped area at or below 1311.632960 um^2, and zero max-slew/max-capacitance violations under the supplied constraints. No tool results establishing those conditions are available here.",
  "functional_boundaries": "The module name, ports, widths, parameter declaration/default, combinational behavior, and all 33 unconstrained input bits are preserved. Control selects ptr1 when one and ptr2 when zero. Both q and the contract's offset are interpreted modulo 256; the rewrite does not substitute an untruncated subtraction. The reconstructed result covers the exact mathematical range -255 through 510 and is encoded modulo 65536. The algebra also holds for other eight-bit base values, although only the default instance is assessed and only that instance reduces q generation to a bit inversion. No clocks, state, assumptions, or don't-cares are introduced."
}
